claims.text: The multilayer coatings contain clearly defined individual layers with differing high-entropy compositions.
Interfaces between chemically and crystallographically distinct layers act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Interface-mediated dislocation pinning slows creep and time-dependent plastic deformation.
Interfaces between alternating high-entropy-alloy layers generate significant misfit dislocations.
Interfaces between alternating layers generate compositional heterogeneities that impede dislocation propagation across layers.
The combination of compositional complexity and interface mismatch creates numerous obstacles to dislocation movement.
Dislocation pinning at layer boundaries delays the onset of creep.
Dislocation pinning at layer boundaries reduces the rate of time-dependent plastic deformation.
Under constant load and elevated temperature, multilayer coatings should have a significantly lower creep rate than homogeneous high-entropy-alloy coatings of equivalent overall composition.
Under constant load and elevated temperature, multilayer coatings should exhibit delayed plastic flow relative to homogeneous high-entropy-alloy coatings of equivalent overall composition.
Dislocation pinning is not enhanced by multiple interfaces in the homogeneous single-phase baseline coating.
The proposed interface-pinning mechanism operates within the service temperature and stress regimes typical of protective coatings.
If individual layers are thinner than a critical value required for effective interface-barrier formation, the creep-resistance effect may diminish.
If applied stress activates deformation mechanisms that overcome interface pinning, the creep-resistance effect may diminish.
The multilayer and homogeneous control coatings should be tested under identical constant-load and elevated-temperature conditions while creep rate and interfacial dislocation behavior are measured.
Failure to observe either a statistically significant creep-rate reduction or evidence of interfacial dislocation pinning relative to the homogeneous control would falsify the hypothesis.
